about: ModelPilot's execution policy (switch_policy.py). Jev predicts the model and effort a task needs; ModelPilot switches there directly only when the expected total cost says it pays. Models, efforts, cache behaviour and the cost model live here so they can change without code. Prices come from the rate files merged by bench.rates().

claude-haiku-4-5-20251001.why_not_candidate: Claude Code sends system-role messages mid-history after the first turn, which Haiku rejects, so a session can't be kept on Haiku (policy_actions.transform_request). Jev's probability for Haiku still counts toward the stronger models being enough.

claude-sonnet-5-5.effort_switch_evidence: Sonnet 5.5 effort changes read the tools and system (7,871-7,873 tokens) and rewrote only the messages (465-504), 8/8 (runs/thinking-probe-sonnet-5-5-20260928-133426); Sonnet 5 had rewritten everything.

claude-opus-5-5.run_factor_evidence: Against Sonnet 5.5 on the same task, both at the client's medium, over the 23 tuning tasks of the fixed arms in bench-20260929-000001 and bench-20260930-161402: 1.25x the main-loop requests and 1.16x the output per request (geometric means).
claude-opus-5-5.effort_switch_evidence: Opus 5.5 effort changes kept tools and system cached and rewrote only the messages (runs/thinking-probe-opus-5-5-effort-20260926-132158).

effort_factor_evidence: Output per request and main-loop requests against medium on the same task. high: Sonnet 5.5 on the 4 tasks the ModelPilot arm ran at high in bench-20261003-095823 (with per-message effort, so the effort held) against fixed Sonnet 5.5 medium in bench-20260930-161402: 1.23x output, 1.33x requests (geometric means; 1.09-1.52 and 1.10-1.83). xhigh: one Opus 5.5 task (cachetools-cached-condition), against fixed Opus 5.5 medium: 1.23x output, 2.12x requests, applied to both models. low and max are unmeasured guesses (max at least xhigh's). The earlier guesses (output only, high 1.6, xhigh 2.4) had no request factor.
defaults_evidence: The shape of a Sonnet 5.5 medium task, pooled over the 23 tuning tasks of fixed Sonnet 5.5 (bench-20260929-000001, bench-20260930-161402): 7.0 main-loop requests, 480 output tokens and 810 other new tokens written to the cache per request (rounded to 500 and 800). For a 7,100-token first request these defaults forecast $0.090 for Sonnet 5.5 medium and $0.218 for Opus 5.5 medium, against $0.085 and $0.219 measured per task (pooled); fed each task set's own measured shape, run_cost gives $0.072 and $0.126 against $0.069 and $0.121 for Sonnet, $0.175 and $0.315 against $0.170 and $0.333 for Opus. The earlier guesses (15 requests, 1,500 and 1,200 tokens) forecast about $0.30, 2.5-4x too high.
bytes_per_token_evidence: Request JSON bytes per token of the first main-loop request: 2.77-2.85 (mean 2.82) over the 30 recorded turn-start decisions of bench-20260929-000001, bench-20261001-185542 and bench-20261003-095823. It was 4, which put prefixes about 30% low.

recovery.redo_on: Jev's recommendation when at least as strong as the failed setting and reachable, else the strongest reachable setting. A failure shows inside the turn, where the effort can't change (effort_changes_at), so reachable means a model at the failed setting's effort: Sonnet 5.5 medium is redone on Opus 5.5 medium, not Opus 5.5 max as before October 3.

hysteresis_scaling: A move must beat staying by hysteresis_usd x P(the current setting is enough): full protection for a plausible current setting, almost none for one that is nearly certain to fail.

step.about: Mid-task decision points (user request, September 29). A step is due when the host-run test suite flips between failing and passing (run_tests results in the ledger), or when the task's measured spend since the last decision reaches overrun_factor x that decision's forecast for the setting it kept or chose. It needs at least min_requests_between billable requests of the task since the last decision, and there are at most max_per_revision per task revision. Candidates are a turn start's plus Jev's effort on the current model, so an effort-only move is always weighed.

return_reuse.about: Price a move to a setting whose own cache entry is still warm (sent within cache_ttl_seconds) and within reach (the conversation has grown by at most max_positions content positions since that setting was last sent) as writing only what that entry doesn't cover. Measured with thinking history in the pinned client's shape (runs/thinking-probe-returns-20260930-091128, $0.4056): returns read the home setting's whole entry 8/8, Sonnet 5.5 effort returns 7 and 25 positions back and Opus 5.5 -> Sonnet 5.5 model returns 8 back. The API documents a 20-position lookback, yet 25 was reached; farther is unmeasured, so it is priced like a first switch.

per_message_effort.about: Effort rides in an effort-only system message (beta mid-conversation-output-config-2026-07-01; Claude Code 2.1.284 already sends its older spelling per-turn-control-2026-07-01) placed after the client's own effort message, which 2.1.284 puts on the system note after the prompt; the top-level effort stays the client's. Every earlier message is put back where it was first sent. Evidence (runs/thinking-probe-per-message-effort-20261001-160146, $0.93): a message at a turn start raised thinking to the native xhigh level at every step with the cache kept; changes inside the tool loop, by message or top-level, changed nothing and also kept the cache (the client's message outranks the top-level effort). So new messages are added only at turn starts (effort_changes_at).

calibration.evidence: Hidden-test passes of the fixed arms on the 23 tuning tasks, both at the client's medium: 16/16 each in bench-20260929-000001 and 7/7 each in bench-20260930-161402. With a uniform prior, (23 + 1) / (23 + 2) = 0.96 for each and for every setting at least as strong.
calibration.about: P_ok at turn starts and steps is (1 - jev_weight) x the measured pass rate of the strongest measured setting the candidate is at least as strong as, plus jev_weight x Jev's estimate; a candidate with no measured setting at or below it (Sonnet 5.5 low) keeps Jev's alone. Jev's estimate read as given had put Sonnet 5.5 medium at 0.02-0.94 on those 23 tasks, all of which it passed. jev_weight is a judgment, not a fit: no tuning task has failed at medium, so there is no evidence yet that Jev's warnings predict a failure. On those 23 tasks (one turn-start answer each), a uniform prior on jev_weight gives a posterior mean of 0.09 and a 95% upper bound of 0.28 (in-sample: the same outcomes set the measured rate), so 0.2 leaves Jev more weight than the outcomes support. Replayed (runs/policy-replay-calibrated-20261003.json), 0.2 keeps all 30 recorded turn starts at Sonnet 5.5 medium; 0.25 jumps on 2, 0.35 on 10. On stuck evidence Jev's estimate is used uncalibrated, conditioned on the current setting failing, since the measured rates can't say which setting rescues a task.

guesses: jev_weight, the low and max effort factors, recovery.wasted_fraction, hysteresis_usd, downgrade_switch_multiplier and the step spacing, cap and overrun factor are starting values, not measurements. The defaults, bytes_per_token, the high and xhigh effort factors, the model factors and the calibration outcomes are measured (see their evidence), on few tasks.
